tables.note: Literal nine table rows;TEM means distinct from optical size; bandgap±0.03eV, uncertainty type unspecified.

source_notes.label: Fresh precursor rather than an aged-sol reconstruction
source_notes.summary: OH-form anion resin is added gradually to0.01M cerium(III)nitrate until pH10.0, then removed by filtration. Fresh sol is immediately treated in half-filled100mLPTFE autoclaves. Earlier sols aged several days and their6–8nm outcome belong to cited study20, not this paper’s nine conditions.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 1–2, Experimental and fresh/aged comparison

source_notes.label: Nine measured temperature/time conditions
source_notes.summary: The table resolves130/150/170°C at30 or180min, and190°C at30/120/180min. TEM means range5.4–6.0nm with no material temperature/time dependence claimed by the authors. Table bandgaps have reported±0.03eV. Physical batches and aliquot overlap are unspecified.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2, Table and Results

source_notes.label: Primary particles and aggregates are distinct
source_notes.summary: Mostly hexagonal particle outlines and occasional chain aggregates are described for cubic CeO2. Figure1 images three named conditions, Figure2 labels eight conditions, and Figure3 DLS curves label four; absent labels are not filled in. DLS sizes are not digitized from curves. Oriented attachment is the authors’ interpretation.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 2–4, TEM/DLS discussion and Figures1–3

source_notes.label: Optical size is not the TEM mean
source_notes.summary: The source uses a cited semiempirical relation to infer a study-level characteristic size of about3.6–3.8nm from bandgap. This remains separate from the table TEM values and is not assigned as a new individual specimen measurement. Coarse CeO2 bandgap about3.2eV is comparison context.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 4, Bandgap discussion, relation from reference26

source_notes.label: Citrate and ATP procedures have different scope
source_notes.summary: Citrate adsorption uses0.1M sodium citrate at0.2–2.0mol/molceria and is most efficient atpH2–5. Filter and wash the sediment, then redisperse to aboutpH9 with NH4OH or NaOH; the NH4OH branch boils off excess ammonia. ATP solution is1% with2mol/LNaOH, amount unspecified. The namedAn-190-30-ATP sample has3.74eV; no new numeric TEM size is supplied.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 1–2,5, Stabilization procedures and named ATP outcome

source_notes.label: Model and biomedical interpretation remain qualified
source_notes.summary: Figure4 is a steric model with two ATP molecules on a(CeO2)70cluster, not a measured particle structure or coordinates. Entire-pH-range ATP stability is qualitative and low-temperature storage is required without a numerical temperature. Sterilization feasibility and mitochondrial affinity are proposed applications, not new measured clinical or cell outcomes.
source_locators: Main PDF p. 4–5, Figure4 and biomedical discussion
